name: The Bur Oak of Elmwood Cemetery

location.address: Historic Elmwood Cemetery, 1200 Elmwood Ave, Detroit, MI 48207 (Bloody Run valley)

access: Free to walk the cemetery grounds, with self-guided tree tour maps on the cemetery's site. Confirm opening hours with the office at 1200 Elmwood Ave before going.
hold: No coordinate, and no source says what separates this oak from others in the Bloody Run valley of an 86-acre cemetery, so no honest recognition line exists. Needs a pin from the cemetery's image-only tree tour PDFs or a reader fix.
transport: By car to 1200 Elmwood Ave on Detroit's east side; bus routes not checked.
story:
By its owner's count, this bur oak was already growing in the 1740s. Historic Elmwood Cemetery puts it at about 280 years and calls it the oldest tree on its grounds. That is one source, but it is the source that owns the ground, and it is the only figure we have found.

It stands in the Bloody Run valley, inside the cemetery. Elmwood became a Level I ArbNet arboretum in 2015, the first in Detroit, and it publishes self-guided tree tour maps for anyone who comes to look at the trunks as well as the graves.

Here is the catch. The cemetery covers about 86 acres and we have no coordinate for this oak yet, so we can give you the valley and not the tree. The tour maps and the office at 1200 Elmwood Avenue are where to ask. If you have stood under it, tell us where, because that is the one thing this page is missing.

Photographs on the cemetery's arboretum page date from Arbor Day 2025, though none of them can be tied to this trunk. Confirm opening hours before you go.

name: The Sweet Gum of Elmwood Cemetery

location.address: Historic Elmwood Cemetery, 1200 Elmwood Ave, Detroit, MI 48207 (Section O, tree no. 657 per register field note)

official_register.name: Michigan Big Tree Register (Michigan Botanical Society)

access: Free to walk the cemetery grounds. Confirm opening hours with the office at 1200 Elmwood Ave before going.
hold: No coordinate: the register's GPS is rounded and falls well outside the cemetery. The recognition line gives the section, but the tree still needs a pin.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as a sweet gum about 2.5 metres round and 23.5 metres tall. It stands in Section O of Elmwood Cemetery, near the spot where four streets meet.
transport: By car to 1200 Elmwood Ave on Detroit's east side; bus routes not checked.
story:
Michigan has exactly one bigger sweet gum, according to the cemetery that owns this one. Historic Elmwood Cemetery calls it the second largest in the state, and the Michigan Big Tree Register holds the numbers. In November 2016 the register recorded a trunk 253 centimetres round and a height of 23.5 metres, with a field note that reads like a treasure map. Section O, near an intersection of four streets, tree number 657.

That note is the best set of directions anybody has written. The register's coordinates are rounded so hard that they land well outside the cemetery, so ignore them and go by the section letter.

The measurements are ten years old now and we have found no report on this trunk since, so read them as the size it was when last checked. Elmwood's arboretum page still names it, which is the most recent word there is.

Nobody has published an age for it. If you know when it was planted, or you have stood beside it lately and can tell us it is still there, we would like to hear.
